components.css: .ds-btn-primary { border: 0; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 999px; padding: 10px 18px; font-family: Quicksand, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; color: #fff; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #ff7aa2, #e84d7d); box-shadow: 0 6px 16px -6px #e84d7d; transition: transform .15s, box-shadow .2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { box-shadow: 0 8px 22px -6px #e84d7d; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(.95); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #c8b6ff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Tiny Button
components.css: .ds-btn-tiny { border: 0; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 999px; padding: 6px 12px; font-family: Quicksand, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; background: #efe9ff; color: #6a4cc2; transition: background .2s; } .ds-btn-tiny:hover { background: #e0d5ff; } .ds-btn-tiny:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #c8b6ff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Chip

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Rounded field with rose stroke; pink on focus.

narrative.overview:
The whole interface is a student's notebook that someone who loves her has decorated. Pages are ruled school paper with a pink margin line. Notes are cream sticky paper tilted a degree or two. A strip of lilac washi tape holds the hero card down. Emoji act as stickers. Headings, the timer and anything "said" by him are in a handwritten face (Patrick Hand), and the working UI stays in a round, legible sans (Quicksand). The page should feel like his handwriting is in the margins of her studies.

Density is relaxed and card-based. Generous rounded white cards float on a pale pink page washed with soft radial blooms of blush, lilac and baby blue. Interaction is soft and bouncy like candy: buttons squish on press, cards lift and tilt slightly on hover, popups pop in with an overshoot. Hearts float up the background, and the brand heart beats. Every animation stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

The look is cute but grown-up: a university student's notebook, not a children's app. It must never read as a cold office tool, with grey, square, dense dashboard chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled-paper, washi-tape and sticky-note materials taken from real stationery
Handwritten display type over a round, friendly sans for the working UI
Pink-led candy pastels, with lilac and mint reserved for meaning
Pill and very round shapes everywhere, softened further by dashed "stitched" borders
Squishy, bouncy micro-interactions that all switch off under reduced motion

rules.name: The Plum Ink Rule
rules.body: Text is never pure black or grey. Body text is plum-ink, secondary text is dusty-plum, and emphasis is raspberry.

rules.name: The Phase Color Rule
rules.body: Mint and violet mean break time and nothing else. Don't use them as decoration elsewhere, or they stop telling her where she is in the cycle.

rules.name: The Handwriting Is His Rule
rules.body: Patrick Hand is for headings and personal or affectionate words. Controls, form fields, data labels and settings stay in Quicksand. The admin content editor deliberately switches the lined textarea back to Quicksand 14px.

rules.name: The Pink Shadow Rule
rules.body: UI shadows are tinted raspberry. Only paper objects (notes, letters) cast neutral shadows, because they are "real" paper stuck onto the page.

rules.name: The Stationery Tilt Rule
rules.body: Only paper objects (notes, letters, tape) rotate at rest, and only by 3° or less. Controls never rotate at rest. They may tilt on hover as a playful response.

dos: Do write anything personal (letters, greetings, reminders, sweet notes) in Patrick Hand, and keep controls in Quicksand.
Do build new surfaces from stationery: ruled paper, sticky-cream notes, washi tape, dashed stitched borders, emoji stickers.
Do keep every interactive element a pill or a very round shape, with the squish (scale .95) on press and a lift or tilt on hover.
Do tint shadows raspberry, and keep neutral drop shadows for paper objects only.
Do dim and lock playful areas while she studies (`body.is-studying`), as the games corner does now.
Do keep the `prefers-reduced-motion` kill-switch covering every new animation.
donts: Don't let it look like an office or SaaS dashboard: no grey palettes, square corners, dense tables or cold neutral chrome.
Don't make it childish. It's a university student's notebook, so keep type sizes, density and copy grown-up rather than toy-like.
Don't use pure black or grey text. Use plum-ink and dusty-plum.
Don't use break mint or rest violet for decoration. They mean break phases.
Don't add competing motion near the timer while she studies. One gentle pulse is the ceiling.
